chapter.title: Rexx Classes that Extend Python Classes
chapter.para: Many Python libraries are used by subclassing: you write a class that extends one of theirs, and they call your methods. With the bridge, that class is a Rexx class.

section.title: A Handler Written in Rexx
section.para: You want Python's HTML parser to call your Rexx code for each tag.

How it works. The class is a subclass of PyObject, and its activate class method calls .py~extend(self, base), with the base as a dotted name. From then on its methods override the base's: HTMLParser's feed calls handle_starttag, which is the Rexx method. Python passes the arguments as it would to its own method: here the tag, and the attributes as a list of pairs.

section.title: A Thread, and a Sequence
section.para: You want a Python thread whose work is a Rexx method, and a Python sequence whose items a Rexx method computes.
How it works. threading.Thread's start runs run on a new thread: the Rexx method, which Python calls on its thread. Worker has no init: new's arguments, the keyword name here, go to the base.

collections.abc.Sequence needs __getitem__ and __len__, and makes in, reversed and iteration from them. init keeps the size, then calls self~init:super, which makes the Python object: until then there is none. A sequence ends with IndexError, which .py~raise raises; it reaches Python as itself.

section.title: Methods on a str or an int
section.para: You want Rexx methods on a value Python sees as a str or an int.

How it works. An immutable object gets its value when it is made: self~init:super("<" || name || ">") passes it to str's __new__. The object is a str in Python, whose text Rexx's || joins, and a Tag in Rexx, with close. Celsius has no init, so 100 goes to int; in fahrenheit, self * 9 is Python's multiplication of the int.
